questions.q: They who are in this room / should not move from the place / where they are standing, said the / leader of the criminals.
questions.s:
Explanation:- Relative Pronoun se pehle 'they' ka demonstrative Version likha jaata hai isliye yahan 'they' nahi 'those' ka use kiya jayega, yeh baat aapko yaad hi karni hai. Bas dhyan rakhiyega Introductory Subject 'It' wale jo sentence hote hai.

For example :- It is they who took you to hospital.

Yahan par 'They' hi rahega isme 'Those' nahi karna hai.

o: B) if none of them knew it
C) that no one of them knew it
A) whether either of them knew it

questions.s: When referring to two people or things, 'neither' is the correct word to use for a negative sense instead of 'no one'.

questions.q: The car I bought last week is already showing signs of wear and tear.
o: The car I bought last week
signs of wear and tear.
questions.s:
Relative pronouns (who/which/that) are used as a subject in subordinate clauses. So, the correct option would be (a) The car I bought last week.

Here's the corrected version: "The car that I bought last week is already showing signs of wear and tear."

questions.q: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’.
o: I and my friends are planned
Me and my friends have plan
No improvement required
My friends and I are planning
questions.s:
Explanation:

  • The original sentence: “Me and my friends planning a road trip…” is grammatically incorrect.

  • It lacks a helping verb and also uses “Me” as the subject, which is incorrect.

  • Correct structure requires:

  • Proper subject order: “My friends and I” (not “Me and my friends”)

  • Correct verb form: “are planning” (present continuous)

✅ So, the improved sentence is:
“My friends and I are planning a road trip to the beach this weekend.”

questions.s:
Either denotes a choice between two. ‘Any’ and ‘one’ is used for many persons or things.

The corrected sentence should be: "Either of these two restaurants would be a good choice for dinner tonight."

questions.q:
You and I / have submitted / your work / on time.

(SSC CGL Tier-01 21/04/22)
questions.s:
Correct Answer: Your work

"your work" is wrong because "You and I" means it is a group effort. "Your" shows that the work belongs to only one person, which is incorrect here.

"Your" is a second-person possessive adjective, used to refer to something belonging to the person addressed.

The work belongs to both "You and I," so the correct possessive determiner is "our" or a neutral determiner like "the.”

Correct Sentence:

1. "You and I have submitted our work on time."

OR

2. "You and I have submitted the work on time."

questions.q: Q22. 39. I asked the two students if <u>anyone of them</u> had completed the assignment.
questions.s: Do logo ke liye 'neither' ya 'either' ka use hota hai. Use 'neither' or 'either' when referring to exactly two people.
